title: Curated first-party X handle allowlist
summary: Third and final queued #3 enhancement. Added a curated first-party X handle allowlist (config/curated-x-handles.json) covering builders/researchers such as Andrej Karpathy, Simon Willison, Chip Huyen and others, plus a tested helper (loadCuratedXHandles + markCuratedXHandles) that tags builder_observation candidates whose handle matches as curated_first_party. The builders collection applies the tag before returning, so when a curated handle surfaces in the follow-builders feed or builder search it is marked as first-party signal for prioritization. This is the canonical curated list the diagnosis said was missing and the extension point for the future; it is honest about the platform limit: X has no free API, so feed-less handles (a researcher X timeline that never appears in the aggregated feed) are not magically ingested by this change. Their blogs are already covered by the builder fallback RSS sources.

lessons.lesson: A curated first-party handle list is an allowlist plus prioritization, not an ingestion path on a platform with no free API.
lessons.evidence: The builder candidate already carries a handle from the aggregated feed; tagging matched handles as curated_first_party is deterministic and testable, while actually pulling a feed-less handle's timeline still requires a paid API or a maintained scraper.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep the curated list in config and tag matching candidates; add a per-handle feed_url only when a reliable feed exists, and do not claim timeline ingestion without an API.

followups.action: Let selection prioritize curated_first_party builder candidates (keep them above low-signal builders), and surface enriched GitHub Trending topics/license tags in the public cards.
